analysis: Reviewed docs/developer/test.md head excerpts (lines 4007-4879) and landing/package-lock.json metadata. The test.md changes are documentation-only: GPT-OSS checkpoint restart/mixed-prefix live fixtures, model prefix benchmarks, Qwen retention, connected cache HTTP gates, App Attest qualification, and other test run instructions. No executable source, auth, attestation, encryption, billing, or runtime config changed. The docs reference T-041 prefix-cache properties (encrypted SSD checkpoints, tenant isolation, ephemeral test keys, isolated temp roots). They state the tests use ephemeral keys, never touch production DB/Privy/Stripe secrets, and make no production attestation or keychain claims, so they do not contradict T-041 mitigations. Commands use disposable DATABASE_URL and warn against production databases. The landing/package-lock.json entry has no patch or text, only metadata with modes unchanged (100644), so dependency changes could not be examined. That is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. The landing page is also not a modeled trust boundary. Downstream passes should check whether lockfile changes accompany any package.json or dependency updates in other units.
